newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks recover on bottom-fishing, month-end.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks recover on bottom-fishing, month-end.

text.p: Mexican stocks rebounded from an early fall to close higher Thursday as bargain hunters finally stepped into the market, traders said.
"Domestic and foreign bottom-fishing buyers stepped in. Anyone with cash to buy got rich today," a trader said.
The blue chip IPC index was up 50.84 points, or 1.61 percent, at 3,213.33 points. Volume was very heavy, at 160 million shares traded, although 35 million were accounted for by just one deal.
Other traders and analysts pointed to the fact that many were closing month-end positions, and that the bourse was also hauled up by Mexican ADRs listed in New York.

"The bourse's rebound may be put down to ... the end of month, when dealers always try to push prices up and, when you consider bargain prices, the rally was logical," said Daniel Romo, analyst at the Bancrecer brokerage.

ADRs listed by cement makers Cemex and media group Televisa ended up 1/4 and 5/8, respectively, at 4-1/4 and 26-1/4 in New York, and closed up 75 centavos (9 cents) and 2.00 pesos (25 cents) at 27.25 ($3.41) and 105.00 pesos ($13.16) in Mexico.

On the broad market scoreboard, a total of 110 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 62 to 23. Beverage firm Ggemex headed the leaders, up 50 centavos (6 cents) at 3.00 pesos (38 cents), but at minimal volume.

Construction firm Geo chalked up the second highest percentage gain of the day, up 2.50 pesos (31 cents) to 36.00 ($4.51) boosted by the possibility of an association with South American construction firms.
Corn flour company Gruma was a notable loser, down 2.05 pesos (26 cents) at 39.90 ($5.00), having traded over 18 million shares. Gruma announced a global stock offer during the session.
